label: prf:knot-factor-amphicheiral
title: Proof of knot factor amphicheiral
html:
Proof. Proof of knot factor amphicheiral

Proof. By trace cyclicity, \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) = \chi_\lambda(w\,\beta_\mathcal{K}\, w^{-1}) = \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}) for every \lambda. Substituting in (knot factor) a_\mathcal{K} = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K})\,\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) / \chi_\lambda(\mathbf{1})^2 yields the displayed expression. \square

Worked example (\mathcal{K} = 4_1 in B_3). Take the figure-eight braid \beta_{4_1} = \sigma_1\,\sigma_2^{-1}\,\sigma_1\,\sigma_2^{-1}. Direct computation of the Hoefsmit characters on the three partitions \lambda \vdash 3 at the substrate q_0 gives:

\lambda \chi_\lambda(\beta_{4_1}) \chi_\lambda(\beta_{4_1}^*) match?
(3) +1 +1 yes
(2,1) -1 -1 yes
(1,1,1) +1 +1 yes

All three characters agree, so \beta_{4_1}^* is conjugate to \beta_{4_1} in H_3(q) — i.e. 4_1 is Markov-amphicheiral. The displayed formula therefore applies, with

  a_{4_1} \;=\;
  w_{(3)}\cdot 1
  \;+\; w_{(2,1)}\cdot \tfrac{1}{4}
  \;+\; w_{(1,1,1)}\cdot 1.

This is the alternating-block projection used in the {}^3\mathrm{H} and {}^3\mathrm{He} formulas — not a fitted ansatz.

Note on the historical formulation. An earlier version of this corollary stated \chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}^*) = (-1)^{[\lambda = (1^n)]}\chi_\lambda(\beta_\mathcal{K}) ("sign-flip on the alternating block") and collapsed the formula to a = 1 - h^2 with h := \chi_{(1^n)}/\chi_{(1^n)}(\mathbf{1}). The sign-flip claim is empirically false on 4_1: the 1-dimensional alternating character factors through writhe, which is 0 for both \beta_{4_1} and its mirror, so both compute to +1 rather than to opposite signs. In addition, the collapse to 1 - h^2 silently invoked \sum_{\lambda \neq (1^n)} w_\lambda (\chi_\lambda/\chi_\lambda(\mathbf{1}))^2 = 1, which is a Cauchy–Schwarz bound, not an identity. The Markov-amphicheirality framework above replaces both defects with a single, structural condition (conjugacy of \beta_K^* to \beta_K in H_n) that 4_1 in fact satisfies, and gives the clean sum-of-positive-squares formula. See the computational verification in the canonical formalism.
